scenarios.desc: Find every caller of a Python function
scenarios.input: I need every caller of resolve_artifact_root defined in src/claude/lib/paths.py before I change its signature. Serena is active in this session. How do I find them? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Tier 1: when Serena is active use find_symbol and find_referencing_symbols. The When it applies section says a symbol search in a programming-language file uses those tools, not Grep or a symbol-shaped Glob.

scenarios.input: I need to understand scripts/validation/check_push_lock_paths.py, a large Python file, to change one function. Serena is active. How do I read it without loading the whole file? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: When it applies: reading a code file means calling get_symbols_overview (or a navigation tool) first, then reading only the symbol needed, not the whole file.

scenarios.desc: Serena not active, native LSP on Claude harness
scenarios.input: Serena reports no active project in this session. I need the definition of build_rules in build/scripts/generate_rules.py and its references. What do I use before falling back to grep? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Tier 2: when Serena is not active use the built-in LSP tool (goToDefinition, findReferences, workspaceSymbol, hover, diagnostics). Tier 3 grep is only for files no LSP can navigate.

scenarios.desc: Delegating an implementation task to a subagent
scenarios.input: I will hand the change to src/claude/lib/paths.py to an implementation subagent. I found the relevant function with Serena. What must the delegation prompt include? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: When it applies, third bullet: subagents cannot reach MCP tools, so the delegator pre-resolves the symbols (file:line) into the delegation prompt.

scenarios.desc: Grep for a flag string across scripts (negative)
scenarios.input: Find every place the literal flag string --dry-run appears across the scripts/**/*.py files. It is an option string, not a symbol name. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: When grep is correct: a pattern that is not a symbol (prose, a flag, a regex, a constant) is a legitimate grep target, so the LSP preference does not apply.

scenarios.desc: Search commit history for a removed function (negative)
scenarios.input: I need to know which commit removed the function parse_legacy_header from a Python module last year. Outline how to find it. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: When grep is correct: git grep for history search. A history question has no live symbol to navigate to, so an LSP query cannot answer it.
